title: Multi-Faceted Evaluation and Mitigation of Emotion Hallucinations in MLLMs
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in open-ended emotion understanding, yet they often generate emotion hallucinations. Evaluating such hallucinations is particularly challenging for two reasons. First, emotion understanding spans multiple cognitive facets, from multimodal perception to psychological reasoning. Second, emotional interpretations are expressed in free-form language, making existing closed-ended protocols insufficient for evaluation. To address these challenges, we introduce EHR (Emotion Hallucination Rate), an evaluator that quantifies emotion hallucinations across six facets: expression, action, audio, instinct, logic, and conclusion. Using EHR, we reveal that existing mitigation methods often reduce hallucinations in some facets while aggravating them in others, exposing the limitation of coarse-grained correction and the need for facet-aware localization and mitigation. Motivated by this finding, we propose HMER (Hallucination-aware Memory-guided Emotion Reasoning), a training-free framework for emotion hallucination mitigation. HMER maintains a Hallucination Memory that records localized hallucinated claims and enables targeted logit rectification, together with an Anchor Memory that preserves reliable intermediate reasoning states to stabilize subsequent generation. By selectively suppressing unreliable cues while preserving trustworthy reasoning context, HMER enables fine-grained mitigation across diverse hallucination facets. Extensive experiments on 19 MLLMs demonstrate the prevalence of emotion hallucinations and the effectiveness of our framework across diverse model architectures.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses emotion hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by proposing two solutions: EHR, an evaluator measuring hallucinations across 6 facets (expression, action, audio, instinct, logic, conclusion), and HMER, a training-free mitigation framework using Hallucination Memory and Anchor Memory for targeted logit rectification and reasoning stabilization.
AI.motivation: MLLMs show potential in open-ended emotion understanding but frequently generate emotion hallucinations. Current evaluation methods are insufficient because: (1) emotion understanding spans multiple cognitive facets, and (2) emotional interpretations are expressed in free-form language, making closed-ended evaluation protocols inadequate.
AI.method: The paper proposes two methods: (1) EHR (Emotion Hallucination Rate) - an evaluator quantifying hallucinations across six facets: expression, action, audio, instinct, logic, and conclusion; (2) HMER (Hallucination-aware Memory-guided Emotion Reasoning) - a training-free framework with two memory components: Hallucination Memory (records localized hallucinated claims for targeted logit rectification) and Anchor Memory (preserves reliable intermediate reasoning states to stabilize generation).
AI.result: Experiments on 19 MLLMs demonstrate: (1) the prevalence of emotion hallucinations across models, (2) existing mitigation methods often reduce hallucinations in some facets while aggravating them in others, exposing limitations of coarse-grained correction, and (3) HMER enables fine-grained mitigation across diverse hallucination facets.
AI.conclusion: The paper reveals that facet-aware localization and mitigation is necessary for emotion hallucination control. HMER successfully enables fine-grained mitigation by selectively suppressing unreliable cues while preserving trustworthy reasoning context, proving effective across diverse model architectures.

title: Multimodal Temporal Modeling for Continuous Group Emotion Recognition in Multi-party Dialogues
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 12 tables. To appear in the Companion Proceedings of the 28th ACM International Conference on Multimodal Interaction (ICMI Companion '26)
summary: To realize natural behavior in dialogue agents in multi-party dialogue scenarios, it is important to understand group emotion such as valence and arousal as a whole. Most prior work addressed this task at the utterance level or using a coarse-grained time window, which is not sufficient to capture emotional dynamics. In this study, we formulate continuous recognition of the Group Emotion at a one-second resolution. Moreover, we also introduce the Mixed state, which captures the emotional divergence among participants in the group. We constructed a dataset with frame-level soft labels based on the TEIDAN corpus and propose a multimodal temporal framework that integrates audio and video information using a sliding-window context. Experimental results demonstrate that the temporal Transformer outperforms simple baselines and shows stronger temporal agreement with the ground-truth labels than the LLM-based model. The effect of context length is limited, whereas audio-visual input outperforms either unimodal input on the continuous-label metrics. Additionally, our analysis shows larger Group Emotion recognition errors in intervals with high Mixed values, exposing emotional divergence as a key challenge for group emotion recognition.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses continuous group emotion recognition in multi-party dialogues at one-second resolution, introducing a "Mixed state" to capture emotional divergence among participants. The proposed multimodal temporal framework using Transformer architecture outperforms baselines and LLM-based models, with audio-visual input proving most effective.
AI.motivation: Prior work on group emotion recognition operated at utterance-level or used coarse-grained time windows, which is insufficient for capturing emotional dynamics in natural multi-party dialogue. The need to understand group-level valence and arousal as a continuous process drove this research.
AI.method: The researchers constructed a dataset with frame-level soft labels based on the TEIDAN corpus and proposed a multimodal temporal framework integrating audio and video information using a sliding-window context. They compared a temporal Transformer against baselines and an LLM-based model.
AI.result: The temporal Transformer outperformed simple baselines and showed stronger temporal agreement with ground-truth labels than the LLM-based model. Context length effect was limited, while audio-visual input outperformed either unimodal input on continuous-label metrics. Analysis revealed larger recognition errors in intervals with high Mixed values.
AI.conclusion: Emotional divergence among participants (captured by the Mixed state) represents a key challenge for group emotion recognition. The temporal Transformer approach proves effective for continuous group emotion recognition at fine-grained temporal resolution.

title: ReCHOIR: Contact-guided Human Object Interaction Retargeting to Diverse Characters
summary: We present ReCHOIR, a novel contact-guided motion retargeting method for transferring human object interaction (HOI) motions across diverse humanoid characters. Unlike prior motion retargeting methods that primarily focus on transferring human motion alone, our goal is to preserve not only the semantics of the original body movement but also consistent interaction between the character and the manipulated object, while jointly producing aligned target human and object motions. Given source HOI motion, object geometry, and contact cues extracted from the source interaction, ReCHOIR retargets an HOI sequence to target characters with different skeletal configurations while maintaining both motion semantics and contact-consistent interaction patterns. Our method builds on a Part-Aware Motion Embedding (PAME) autoencoder, which encodes full-body motion into a shared body-part-wise latent space. This representation enables generalization across heterogeneous skeletons while preserving local motion semantics beneficial for part-aware adaptation in HOI retargeting. On top of this representation, we introduce a contact-guided retargeting module and an object motion decoder for HOI retargeting. The contact-guided retargeting module treats the source object interaction as a condition for refining target character motion: object- and contact-related signals are encoded into a body-part-aligned latent representation and injected into decoding through a residual control branch, enabling stronger adaptation in interaction-relevant body regions without discarding the underlying motion prior. In parallel, the object motion decoder predicts a target object motion aligned with the refined target character motion, ensuring that the object trajectory remains consistent with how the interaction is realized by the target character.

AI.tldr: ReCHOIR is a novel contact-guided motion retargeting method for transferring human object interaction (HOI) motions across diverse humanoid characters with different skeletal configurations while preserving motion semantics and contact-consistent interaction patterns.
AI.motivation: Prior motion retargeting methods focus on transferring human motion alone, but fail to preserve consistent interaction between the character and manipulated object. This work addresses the need to jointly produce aligned target human and object motions while maintaining interaction semantics.
AI.method: The method uses a Part-Aware Motion Embedding (PAME) autoencoder that encodes full-body motion into a shared body-part-wise latent space for skeleton generalization. A contact-guided retargeting module treats source object interaction as a condition, encoding object and contact signals into body-part-aligned latent representation and injecting them through a residual control branch. An object motion decoder predicts target object motion aligned with the refined character motion.
AI.result: The method enables generalization across heterogeneous skeletons while preserving local motion semantics for part-aware adaptation in HOI retargeting. It maintains both motion semantics and contact-consistent interaction patterns between character and object.
AI.conclusion: ReCHOIR successfully transfers HOI motions to target characters with different skeletal configurations while preserving interaction semantics and producing aligned object motions, addressing a key limitation in prior motion retargeting approaches.

title: Sparse Weight and Edge Circuit Discovery in Transformer-based Acoustic Models
summary: Transformer-based foundation models are powerful but opaque, motivating Mechanistic Interpretation methods to uncover the black-box by identifying small computation subgraphs responsible for a task. DiscoGP is a joint weight-and-edge circuit discovery framework originally developed for text decoders. We extend DiscoGP to speech encoders and present, to our knowledge, the first circuit discovery study for modern speech foundation models. Across HuBERT and Wav2Vec 2.0 on several speech classification tasks, we find that the discovered circuits are extremely compact, yet often match or even exceed the performance of the full pretrained encoder with the same downstream head. Through ablations, we show that these circuits reflect pretrained computation rather than random structure or task-head artifacts. We also introduce a memory-efficient DiscoGP variant that reduces the GPU memory cost of edge-circuit discovery at runtime from quartic to cubic. Overall, our results broaden Mechanistic Interpretation beyond text decoders and show that circuit-level analysis can reveal both explanatory structure and unexpected functional behavior in speech encoders.

AI.tldr: This paper extends DiscoGP (a circuit discovery framework) from text decoders to speech encoders, presenting the first circuit discovery study for modern speech foundation models (HuBERT and Wav2Vec 2.0). The discovered circuits are extremely compact yet match or exceed full pretrained encoder performance.
AI.motivation: Transformer-based foundation models are powerful but opaque, motivating Mechanistic Interpretation methods to uncover the black-box by identifying computation subgraphs responsible for tasks. This study aims to extend circuit discovery beyond text decoders to speech encoders.
AI.method: DiscoGP (joint weight-and-edge circuit discovery framework) was extended to speech encoders. Experiments were conducted across HuBERT and Wav2Vec 2.0 on several speech classification tasks. Ablations were performed to verify circuits reflect pretrained computation. A memory-efficient variant was introduced to reduce GPU memory cost from quartic to cubic.
AI.result: Discovered circuits are extremely compact yet often match or exceed the performance of the full pretrained encoder with the same downstream head. Ablations confirm circuits reflect pretrained computation rather than random structure or task-head artifacts.
AI.conclusion: Circuit-level analysis can reveal both explanatory structure and unexpected functional behavior in speech encoders. This broadens Mechanistic Interpretation beyond text decoders, enabling interpretability research for speech foundation models.

title: M3-Former: Multimodal Transformer with Mixture-of-Experts for Long-Term Vessel Trajectory Prediction
summary: To address the challenges of behavioral multimodality, limited semantic utilization, and long-term error accumulation in vessel trajectory prediction, this paper proposes M3-Former, a multimodal trajectory prediction framework enhanced by large language models (LLMs). The proposed framework incorporates vessel static attributes and navigational intent as semantic priors for long-term trajectory modeling. Specifically, a unified multimodal representation space is constructed, in which static semantic information is encoded by a pre-trained LLM and aligned with dynamic trajectory features through self-attention. To jointly capture global route planning and local motion variations, a dual-granularity Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture is introduced, where sequence-level experts model global navigation trends and token-level experts refine fine-grained maneuvering behaviors. In addition, a Steering-Weighted Cross-Entropy loss is designed to alleviate the long-tail distribution of sparse turning samples and improve prediction accuracy in critical maneuvering scenarios. Experiments on a real-world Danish AIS dataset demonstrate that M\textsuperscript{3}-Former consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across prediction horizons from 1 to 4 hours. In the 4-hour prediction task, the proposed method reduces Average Displacement Error (ADE) and Final Displacement Error (FDE) by 4.4\% and 5.1\%, respectively, compared with the strongest baseline. Qualitative and ablation analyses further verify that semantic fusion effectively reduces long-term trajectory drift, while the dual-granularity MoE improves robustness in complex waterways and route-branching scenarios. The proposed framework establishes a semantic-guided hierarchical prediction paradigm, in which high-level navigational intent and local motion dynamics are jointly modeled for robust long-term vessel trajectory forecasting.

AI.tldr: M3-Former is a multimodal vessel trajectory prediction framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to address behavioral multimodality, limited semantic utilization, and long-term error accumulation. It uses semantic priors from vessel static attributes and navigational intent, combined with a dual-granularity Mixture-of-Experts architecture and a custom Steering-Weighted Cross-Entropy loss. The method outperforms baselines on a Danish AIS dataset, reducing ADE by 4.4% and FDE by 5.1% for 4-hour predictions.
AI.motivation: The challenges being addressed are: 1) Behavioral multimodality in vessel trajectories, 2) Limited semantic utilization in existing methods, and 3) Long-term error accumulation in trajectory prediction. These issues make long-term vessel trajectory forecasting unreliable, especially in critical maneuvering scenarios and complex waterways.
AI.method: The proposed M3-Former framework employs: 1) A unified multimodal representation space where static semantic information is encoded by a pre-trained LLM and aligned with dynamic trajectory features via self-attention; 2) A dual-granularity MoE architecture with sequence-level experts modeling global navigation trends and token-level experts refining fine-grained maneuvering behaviors; 3) A Steering-Weighted Cross-Entropy loss designed to address the long-tail distribution of sparse turning samples.
AI.result: Experiments on a real-world Danish AIS dataset show M3-Former consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across prediction horizons from 1 to 4 hours. In the 4-hour prediction task, ADE and FDE are reduced by 4.4% and 5.1% respectively compared to the strongest baseline. Qualitative and ablation analyses confirm semantic fusion reduces long-term trajectory drift, while dual-granularity MoE improves robustness in complex waterways and route-branching scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The framework establishes a semantic-guided hierarchical prediction paradigm that jointly models high-level navigational intent and local motion dynamics for robust long-term vessel trajectory forecasting. The integration of LLMs for semantic encoding, dual-granularity expert modeling, and the custom loss function effectively addresses the identified challenges in multimodal trajectory prediction.

title: Probabilistic Focal Search: Accelerating Bounded-Suboptimal Search via Lower-Bound Advancement
summary: Bounded-suboptimal search seeks a solution within a factor $w$ of optimal while reducing search effort. Focal Search (FS) uses heuristic guidance within FOCAL, the frontier nodes eligible under the threshold $w f_{\min}$, but its deterministic policy may leave $f_{\min}$ unchanged for many expansions. We introduce Probabilistic Focal Search (PFS), which follows the FS guided choice with probability $p$ and expands a minimum-$f$ OPEN node with probability $1-p$. The latter branch encourages the lower bound to advance, enlarging FOCAL and admitting nodes that may lead to feasible solutions. By balancing guidance and lower-bound advancement, this mechanism can reduce time to a bounded solution when progress is limited by delayed FOCAL admission. As a secondary transfer experiment, we apply the same scheduler to Dynamic Potential Search, yielding Probabilistic Dynamic Potential Search (PDPS). We benchmark PFS against FS on N-Puzzle, Pancake Sorting, and the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), and evaluate its anytime extension on the Generalized Covering TSP (GCTSP), using multiple $w$ and $p$ values. Across these benchmarks, the largest gains occur when long $f_{\min}$ plateaus delay useful FOCAL admissions; in such settings, the probabilistic factor may reduce node expansions by about 90\% or more (e.g., on N-Puzzle and TSP). For the anytime algorithm family, Anytime Probabilistic Focal Search (APFS) outperforms all tested algorithms in evaluating anytime methods on GCTSP. We also observe that the benefit is smaller when the deterministic search already advances efficiently (e.g., Pancake Sorting), indicating that the probabilistic factor is most useful when FOCAL admission is a search bottleneck. The PDPS transfer shows that the mechanism also transfers to potential guidance, although its common-success effects remain domain- and bound-dependent.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Probabilistic Focal Search (PFS), which adds a probabilistic component to Focal Search by occasionally expanding minimum-f OPEN nodes (with probability 1-p) to advance the lower bound and enlarge FOCAL, rather than always following the deterministic heuristic guidance. The approach also transfers to Dynamic Potential Search (PDPS) and includes an anytime variant (APFS).
AI.motivation: Focal Search (FS) uses heuristic guidance within FOCAL (frontier nodes eligible under threshold w f_min), but its deterministic policy may leave f_min unchanged for many expansions, causing delayed FOCAL admission when progress is limited. This bottleneck prevents efficient bounded-suboptimal search.
AI.method: PFS modifies FS by following the FS guided choice with probability p and expanding a minimum-f OPEN node with probability 1-p. The latter branch advances the lower bound, enlarging FOCAL and admitting nodes that may lead to feasible solutions. This mechanism is also applied to Dynamic Potential Search (yielding PDPS) and extended to anytime setting (APFS).
AI.result: Across N-Puzzle, Pancake Sorting, and TSP benchmarks with multiple w and p values, the largest gains occur when long f_min plateaus delay useful FOCAL admissions—in such settings, node expansions can be reduced by about 90% or more (e.g., N-Puzzle and TSP). For GCTSP, APFS outperforms all tested anytime algorithms. The benefit is smaller when deterministic search already advances efficiently (e.g., Pancake Sorting). PDPS shows the mechanism transfers to potential guidance, though effects are domain- and bound-dependent.
AI.conclusion: The probabilistic factor is most useful when FOCAL admission is a search bottleneck. By balancing guidance and lower-bound advancement, PFS can significantly reduce node expansions and time to bounded solutions in domains with long f_min plateaus. The mechanism transfers to other search algorithms (PDPS) but effectiveness varies by domain and bound.

title: When Passing Tests Hides Vulnerabilities: An Empirical Study of Silent Failures in Agentic Systems
summary:
LLM-based agents for automated code repair have received significant attention in recent years from both research and software engineering practice perspectives. However, limited attention has been paid to patches that pass syntactic and functional verification but still retain or introduce security vulnerabilities. The aim of this research is to systematically identify and categorize such silent failures in LLM-based agentic code repair.
  We conducted an empirical study using 1,030 valid execution traces produced by seven agent frameworks with GPT-4o-mini across two security-focused datasets, SecurityEval and CVEfixes. Through three iterations of qualitative coding and manual verification, 170 confirmed silent failures were identified. The key results are: (i) Three main categories of silent failures were identified: Omission, Introduction, and Inadequacy. Omission accounts for 48.2% of the confirmed failures, Introduction for 30.6%, and Inadequacy for 21.2%. (ii) Ten fine-grained failure codes were classified under these three categories, showing how agents omit required security controls, apply incomplete defenses, or introduce new vulnerabilities during repair. (iii) Current test-passing evaluation and LLM-based reviewer roles were insufficient to expose or intercept these failures in the confirmed cases. (iv) Similar insecure solutions appeared across different frameworks, suggesting possible shared model-, prompt-, or task-level influences, while single-agent and multi-agent systems showed different failure profiles.
  The results of this study will assist researchers and practitioners in improving the evaluation of LLM-based agentic code repair and developing targeted verification methods that go beyond functional correctness and cover all generated artifacts.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies and categorizes "silent failures" in LLM-based agentic code repair—patches that pass syntactic and functional verification but still contain security vulnerabilities. Through an empirical study of 1,030 execution traces across 7 agent frameworks using GPT-4o-mini, the authors identified 170 confirmed silent failures across three categories: Omission (48.2%), Introduction (30.6%), and Inadequacy (21.2%). The study reveals that current test-passing evaluation methods are insufficient to detect these security issues.
AI.motivation: While LLM-based agents for automated code repair have gained significant attention, there has been limited research on patches that pass functional verification but still contain security vulnerabilities. The motivation is to systematically identify and categorize these "silent failures" to improve evaluation methods and develop targeted verification approaches beyond functional correctness.
AI.method: The researchers conducted an empirical study using 1,030 valid execution traces produced by seven agent frameworks with GPT-4o-mini across two security-focused datasets (SecurityEval and CVEfixes). They performed three iterations of qualitative coding and manual verification to identify and categorize silent failures.
AI.result: The study identified 170 confirmed silent failures. Three main categories were found: Omission (48.2%) - agents omit required security controls; Introduction (30.6%) - agents introduce new vulnerabilities; and Inadequacy (21.2%) - agents apply incomplete defenses. Ten fine-grained failure codes were classified. Current test-passing evaluation and LLM-based reviewers were insufficient to detect these failures. Similar insecure patterns appeared across different frameworks, while single-agent and multi-agent systems showed different failure profiles.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals that current evaluation methods for LLM-based agentic code repair are inadequate for detecting security vulnerabilities. The results will help researchers and practitioners improve evaluation approaches and develop targeted verification methods that go beyond functional correctness to cover security aspects of generated artifacts.

title: Rethinking Handwritten Character Recognition
summary: Non-Latin handwritten character recognition (HCR) remains understudied. Dominant methods consider it as generic image classification, which uses model scale to implicitly learn stroke structure. Structural-prior efficiency---the principle that explicitly encoding script-geometric regularities as architectural inductive biases can be both more accurate and require fewer parameters. We introduce GraphemeNet, a unified multi-script architecture, governed by two orthogonal binary axes. Axis 1 operationalises stroke-level geometric regularity via Persistent Scaffold Injection (PSI): a script-specific asymmetric convolution injects a stroke scaffold as a weighted residual at every encoder stage, continuously anchoring learned features to script geometry---distinct from skip connections, auxiliary losses, or attention reweighting. Axis 2 selects between global average pooling with gated fusion and cross-scale attention with a Stroke Topology Module (STM), depending on whether glyph discrimination requires spatial relational reasoning. A Linear Capsule Routing (LCR) with $O(n)$ routing is shared universally. On fourteen benchmarks across eight writing systems, the architecture generalises with only scaffold and decoder topology varying per script, consistently challenging, outperforming published baselines, and establishing structural-prior efficiency as a broadly applicable principle for multi-script HCR.

AI.tldr: GraphemeNet introduces a unified multi-script architecture for non-Latin handwritten character recognition (HCR) that leverages structural-prior efficiency—explicitly encoding script-geometric regularities as architectural inductive biases to achieve better accuracy with fewer parameters than generic image classification approaches.
AI.motivation: Non-Latin handwritten character recognition remains understudied. Existing dominant methods treat HCR as generic image classification, relying on large model scale to implicitly learn stroke structure. This approach is inefficient and fails to leverage the inherent geometric regularities specific to each writing system. The authors propose that explicitly encoding script-geometric regularities as architectural inductive biases (structural-prior efficiency) can achieve better accuracy with fewer parameters.
AI.method: GraphemeNet uses two orthogonal binary axes: (1) Persistent Scaffold Injection (PSI) - a script-specific asymmetric convolution that injects a stroke scaffold as a weighted residual at every encoder stage, continuously anchoring learned features to script geometry; (2) A choice between global average pooling with gated fusion or cross-scale attention with a Stroke Topology Module (STM), depending on whether glyph discrimination requires spatial relational reasoning. A Linear Capsule Routing (LCR) with O(n) routing is shared universally across scripts.
AI.result: The architecture was evaluated on fourteen benchmarks across eight writing systems. It consistently outperformed published baselines while using only scaffold and decoder topology varying per script, demonstrating strong generalization capability.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes structural-prior efficiency as a broadly applicable principle for multi-script HCR. The key insight is that explicitly encoding script-specific geometric regularities as architectural inductive biases outperforms implicit learning through model scaling, achieving better accuracy with fewer parameters. This unified architecture can generalize across multiple writing systems with minimal script-specific modifications.

title: Learning Realistic Athletic Sprinting Without Demonstrations
summary: We present a muscle-driven simulation system for generating biomechanically accurate motion for high-speed athletic locomotion tasks that does not require motion demonstrations. Our approach integrates state-of-the-art biomechanical athlete models into a new, high-performance GPU simulator capable of running at 1000x real-time. High-throughput simulation enables large-batch reinforcement learning to train control policies that operate directly in the model's high-dimensional muscle excitation space, and are guided only by task-specific episode termination conditions and a reward that encourages maximizing speed while reducing forces needed to respect joint limits. These policies train within a few hours on a single GPU and generate "near visually realistic" motions for complete athletic activities such as a full 100-meter sprint or performing popular athletic locomotion drills like side-shuffling, backpedaling, and carioca. The generated sprinting motions also exhibit strong agreement with experimental data captured from sprinters.

AI.tldr: A muscle-driven simulation system that generates biomechanically accurate high-speed athletic motions (sprinting, side-shuffling, backpedaling, carioca) using reinforcement learning, without motion demonstrations. Achieves 1000x real-time simulation and trains control policies in hours on a single GPU.
AI.motivation: To generate biomechanically accurate athletic locomotion motions without requiring motion demonstrations, addressing limitations of prior data-driven approaches that depend on captured reference motions.
AI.method: Integrates state-of-the-art biomechanical athlete models into a high-performance GPU simulator (1000x real-time). Uses large-batch reinforcement learning to train control policies operating in the muscle excitation space, guided by task-specific termination conditions and a reward function balancing speed maximization with joint limit force reduction.
AI.result: Policies train within a few hours on a single GPU. Generates "near visually realistic" motions for complete athletic activities including 100m sprint and various drills. Generated sprinting motions show strong agreement with experimental data from sprinters.
AI.conclusion: The approach successfully produces biomechanically plausible high-speed athletic motions through simulation and reinforcement learning, eliminating the need for motion demonstrations while achieving visual realism and experimental validation.

title: Project Qualia: Recovering Experiential Music Structure from Session Co-occurrence Data
summary: This report presents results from Project Qualia, an ongoing effort to determine whether experiential similarity between songs, a structure not captured by genre or metadata taxonomies, can be recovered from real listening behavior. We constructed a large-scale dataset of listening sessions, comprising 1.29 billion scrobbles collected from 9,396 users via the Last.fm API and reduced through a preprocessing pipeline to 531.6 million training scrobbles across 28.6 million sessions. On this corpus, we trained a skip-gram Word2Vec model (Song2Vec), treating each session as a sentence and each track as a token. As anticipated, the resulting embedding space was dominated by artist identity, a consequence of single-artist runs within sessions. To test for a subtler, artist-independent signal, we developed an artist-residual procedure: subtracting each artist's centroid from its tracks' embeddings and evaluating whether the remainder retained structure. Mean cross-artist cosine similarity fell from 0.2487 in raw embedding space to 0.0005 in residual space, yet 4,577 cross-artist track pairs retained cosine similarity $\ge 0.70$ in residual space, forming coherent genre- and era-based clusters, including trip-hop, 1990s grunge, 2020 mainstream pop, and cross-composer classical piano pairs at cosine similarity up to 0.95. These results confirm that the training data contains experiential structure independent of artist identity, establishing an empirical basis for an architecture designed to learn this experiential layer directly.

AI.tldr: Project Qualia investigates whether experiential similarity between songs (beyond genre/metadata) can be recovered from listening behavior. Using 1.29 billion Last.fm scrobbles, Song2Vec (skip-gram Word2Vec) was trained on listening sessions. After removing artist identity bias through artist-residual processing, coherent genre- and era-based clusters (trip-hop, 90s grunge, 2020 pop, classical piano) were found, confirming experiential structure exists independent of artist identity.
AI.motivation: Current music taxonomies (genre, metadata) fail to capture experiential similarity - how songs feel or relate to listeners. This research aims to recover such structure directly from real listening behavior, establishing an empirical basis for architectures that learn experiential layers directly.
AI.method: Collected 1.29 billion scrobbles from 9,396 users via Last.fm API, reduced to 531.6 million training scrobbles across 28.6 million sessions. Trained skip-gram Word2Vec (Song2Vec) treating sessions as sentences and tracks as tokens. To isolate artist-independent signal, developed artist-residual procedure: subtracted each artist's centroid from track embeddings and evaluated residual structure.
AI.result: Raw embedding space showed mean cross-artist cosine similarity of 0.2487 (dominated by artist identity). After residual processing, similarity dropped to 0.0005, yet 4,577 cross-artist track pairs retained similarity ≥ 0.70, forming coherent clusters including trip-hop, 1990s grunge, 2020 mainstream pop, and cross-composer classical piano pairs (similarity up to 0.95).
AI.conclusion: The training data contains experiential structure independent of artist identity. This confirms that listening behavior encodes meaningful similarity information beyond genre or metadata taxonomies, establishing an empirical foundation for architectures designed to learn experiential similarity layers directly.

title: Halo: Improving forecast accuracy through heteroscedastic estimation
summary: Heteroscedastic forecasting, where a network estimates a scale parameter alongside a location parameter, is normally motivated by uncertainty quantification. This paper shows it also improves the point estimate, in contrast to reported negative results for heteroscedastic estimation outside time series. Halo is a modification that reuses an existing deep forecaster's architecture, giving it a second output for the scale of its implied distribution and training it under the matching negative log likelihood. Adapting three state-of-the-art models --- a transformer, a graph network paired with a variational autoencoder, and a single-layer convolutional network --- under both Gaussian and Laplacian losses demonstrates the phenomenon. On the five electricity price markets of a standard forecasting benchmark, Halo improves MSE and MAE in 28 of 30 model-market-metric comparisons, cutting average MSE by 2.6% to 16.5% and average MAE by 1.7% to 11.0%. Two findings emerge: (1) whether the scale estimate comes from a second projection head or from a full parallel network matters far less than whether the network estimates scale, and (2) the improvement holds under the hyperparameters already tuned for the point-estimate baseline, so retuning is optional.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces "Halo," a modification to deep forecasting models that adds a second output for estimating the scale parameter of a distribution, improving both uncertainty quantification and point estimates. The method is tested on three state-of-the-art models across five electricity price markets, achieving improvements in 28 of 30 model-market-metric comparisons.
AI.motivation: Heteroscedastic forecasting (estimating scale alongside location) is typically used for uncertainty quantification. This paper challenges the assumption that it only helps with uncertainty, demonstrating that it also improves point estimates - contrary to reported negative results for heteroscedastic estimation outside time series.
AI.method: Halo reuses an existing deep forecaster's architecture by adding a second output for the scale parameter, training under negative log likelihood. Three state-of-the-art models were adapted: a transformer, a graph network with variational autoencoder, and a single-layer convolutional network. Experiments used both Gaussian and Laplacian losses on five electricity price markets from a standard forecasting benchmark.
AI.result: Halo improved MSE and MAE in 28 of 30 model-market-metric comparisons. Average MSE was reduced by 2.6% to 16.5%, and average MAE by 1.7% to 11.0%. Two key findings: (1) whether scale estimation uses a second projection head or full parallel network matters less than whether scale is estimated at all; (2) improvements hold without retuning hyperparameters already tuned for baseline point estimates.
AI.conclusion: Heteroscedastic forecasting through Halo consistently improves point estimates in time series forecasting. The method is robust across different model architectures and loss functions, and does not require hyperparameter retuning. The choice between projection head vs. parallel network is less important than simply adding scale estimation.

title: Automating Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) Formulation Generation from Natural Language
comment: Accepted at the ICML 2026 Workshop on AI as a Tool for Mathematics, Computer Science, and Machine Learning (AI4Research)
summary: Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) is a central formulation for combinatorial optimization and has gained increasing attention due to its compatibility with quantum, hybrid quantum-classical, and quantum-inspired solvers. However, translating natural-language problem descriptions into correct QUBO formulations remains difficult, requiring the identification of binary variables, constraints, objective functions, penalty terms, and suitable penalty weights. This process is time-consuming and often demands substantial domain expertise. To address this challenge, we propose an end-to-end multi-agent framework that automatically generates QUBO formulations from natural-language problem descriptions, supported by structured or unstructured test cases. To evaluate its performance, We also introduce QUBOBench, a benchmark containing 100 combinatorial optimization problems across 12 application domains, curated from peer-reviewed literature, competitions, and canonical NP-hard problems. Experimental results show that our framework achieves 68% accuracy on QUBOBench, outperforming a direct single-call baseline by 22%. Further analysis identifies iterative self-repair as the most important component contributing to improved performance. The data and code are open-sourced at https://quitttcat.github.io/QuantumQUBOAgent.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an end-to-end multi-agent framework that automatically generates QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) formulations from natural-language problem descriptions, accompanied by QUBOBench—a benchmark of 100 combinatorial optimization problems across 12 domains. The framework achieves 68% accuracy, outperforming a baseline by 22%, with iterative self-repair identified as the most critical component.
AI.motivation: Translating natural-language problem descriptions into correct QUBO formulations is challenging, time-consuming, and requires substantial domain expertise. The process involves identifying binary variables, constraints, objective functions, penalty terms, and suitable penalty weights—making it difficult for users without specialized knowledge to leverage QUBO solvers.
AI.method: The authors propose a multi-agent framework that automatically generates QUBO formulations from natural-language problem descriptions, supported by structured or unstructured test cases. They also introduce QUBOBench, a benchmark containing 100 combinatorial optimization problems across 12 application domains, curated from peer-reviewed literature, competitions, and canonical NP-hard problems.
AI.result: The framework achieves 68% accuracy on QUBOBench, outperforming a direct single-call baseline by 22%. Further analysis identifies iterative self-repair as the most important component contributing to improved performance.
AI.conclusion: The proposed multi-agent framework successfully automates QUBO formulation generation with significant accuracy improvements over baseline approaches. The introduced QUBOBench benchmark provides a valuable evaluation standard for future research in this area. The data and code are open-sourced.

title: Optimizing AI Inference Across the Deployment Stack
summary: AI deployment performance is shaped not by model architecture alone, but by interactions among compression, compiler transformations, and serving policies. Published benchmarks often report latency and throughput under incomparable conditions, limiting their use for deployment decisions. This paper presents a unified analytical treatment of inference optimization across the deployment stack. We introduce a three-layer taxonomy covering model-level techniques such as quantization, pruning, and distillation; compiler transformations such as graph fusion, layout optimization, and kernel autotuning; and system policies such as dynamic batching, admission control, and memory tiering. We formulate deployment as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem over accuracy, latency, throughput, memory footprint, and energy, and analyze a deployment-ranking functional with Pareto monotonicity and scale invariance. Roofline models show how memory-bandwidth hierarchies bound performance across precision regimes, while queuing models explain how service-time changes amplify response time under load. To improve comparability, we propose an evidence protocol that separates measured, derived, and analytical claims; limits numerical comparison to within-paper results; and requires reporting of hardware, software versions, batch semantics, and thermal state. We synthesize evidence from edge platforms, including Jetson AGX Orin and five inference frameworks; data center GPUs, including A100 and H100 with three LLM serving engines; and quantization studies across the Llama-3.1 family. The synthesis shows that deployment outcomes are governed by cross-layer interactions that no single-layer analysis can predict. We conclude with a constraint-aware selection procedure and open problems in compiler-serving co-optimization, cross-hardware performance prediction, and standardized energy reporting.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified analytical framework for AI inference optimization across the entire deployment stack, addressing the problem that published benchmarks report incomparable performance metrics. The authors introduce a three-layer taxonomy (model compression, compiler transformations, system policies) and formulate deployment as a multi-objective optimization problem.
AI.motivation: The core problem is that existing benchmarks report latency and throughput under incomparable conditions, making them unsuitable for deployment decisions. The authors argue that AI deployment performance is shaped by interactions among compression, compiler transformations, and serving policies—not just model architecture alone.
AI.method: 1) Three-layer taxonomy covering model-level techniques (quantization, pruning, distillation), compiler transformations (graph fusion, layout optimization, kernel autotuning), and system policies (dynamic batching, admission control, memory tiering); 2) Formulation as constrained multi-objective optimization over accuracy, latency, throughput, memory footprint, and energy; 3) Deployment-ranking functional with Pareto monotonicity and scale invariance; 4) Roofline models for memory-bandwidth analysis and queuing models for service-time analysis; 5) Evidence protocol for standardized reporting; 6) Empirical validation across edge platforms (Jetson AGX Orin), data center GPUs (A100, H100), and Llama-3.1 quantization studies.
AI.result: The synthesis demonstrates that deployment outcomes are governed by cross-layer interactions that no single-layer analysis can predict. Key findings include: memory-bandwidth hierarchies bound performance across precision regimes; service-time changes amplify response time under load; and cross-layer interactions are critical for deployment optimization.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes with: 1) A constraint-aware selection procedure for deployment decisions; 2) Three open problems: compiler-serving co-optimization, cross-hardware performance prediction, and standardized energy reporting. The work emphasizes the need for comparable benchmarks and cross-layer optimization approaches.

title: AcFlow: Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion Transformers via Learned Conditional Activation Flow
summary: Text-to-image diffusion transformers (DiTs) are powerful generators, yet direct prompting provides limited control interface for style intensity and can fail to suppress unwanted concepts. To enable these controls, we introduce AcFlow, an inference-time controller that transports intermediate layer image-token activations through a learned concept-conditioned velocity field while keeping the base DiT frozen. A textual concept description specifies the desired intervention, while the integration horizon provides a continuous control parameter. The field produces token-varying, activation-dependent updates. With parameters shared across concepts within each task family, the field supports fine-grained descriptions and generalizes to concepts unseen during training without per-concept fitting. On style control, AcFlow achieves the best style--content trade-off among the evaluated baselines in the high-style-alignment regime. At a fixed operating point, AcFlow attains style--content alignment of 0.5365/0.2860, compared with 0.4397/0.2684 for the baseline with the highest style alignment. Qualitative results demonstrate suppression of diverse concepts, including cases where direct prompting fails. Our analyses support the learned velocity field as an adaptive control mechanism, with update directions varying across tokens and depend on their activation states. Our code is available at https://github.com/Nove1yst/AcFlow.

AI.tldr: AcFlow is an inference-time controller for text-to-image diffusion transformers (DiTs) that modifies intermediate layer activations through a learned concept-conditioned velocity field to enable style intensity control and concept suppression without fine-tuning the base model.
AI.motivation: Direct prompting in text-to-image diffusion transformers provides limited control over style intensity and cannot effectively suppress unwanted concepts. There is a need for an inference-time control mechanism that offers fine-grained control without modifying the underlying model.
AI.method: AcFlow uses a learned concept-conditioned velocity field that operates on intermediate layer image-token activations. The controller takes a textual concept description as input and uses an integration horizon as a continuous control parameter. The velocity field produces token-varying, activation-dependent updates with parameters shared across concepts within each task family, enabling generalization to unseen concepts without per-concept fitting.
AI.result: AcFlow achieves the best style-content trade-off among evaluated baselines in the high-style-alignment regime. At a fixed operating point, AcFlow attains style-content alignment of 0.5365/0.2860 compared to 0.4397/0.2684 for the baseline with highest style alignment. Qualitative results demonstrate suppression of diverse concepts where direct prompting fails.
AI.conclusion: The learned velocity field serves as an adaptive control mechanism with update directions varying across tokens and depending on their activation states. AcFlow enables fine-grained control through textual concept descriptions and generalizes to unseen concepts without requiring per-concept fitting.

title: Gaussian Light Transport
comment: To appear in SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 (Conference Track). 11 pages, 8 figures. Project page: https://patrick-attimont.com/projects/gaussian-light-transport/
summary: We present a novel method for computing global illumination by expressing the solution to the light transport equation as a 13D Gaussian mixture model over positions, directions, surface normals, and material properties. We show that including scene properties in the Gaussian representation drastically reduces the number of functions and speeds up evaluation. As opposed to traditional light transport methods based on Neumann series, the parameters of our model are directly estimated by minimizing the residual of the rendering equation. While both optimization and rendering require repeated evaluations of a linear combination of high-dimensional Gaussian functions, we introduce an efficient culling strategy to keep the optimization tractable and produce renderings in real time. Our representation enables to render fast, view-independent solutions to the light transport equation, achieving rendering times on the order of milliseconds, with a fraction of the memory requirements of conventional neural rendering approaches.

AI.tldr: A novel global illumination method using a 13D Gaussian mixture model that encodes position, direction, surface normal, and material properties, enabling real-time view-independent rendering with lower memory requirements than neural approaches.
AI.motivation: Traditional light transport methods based on Neumann series are computationally expensive. Neural rendering approaches, while effective, have high memory requirements. The authors seek a more efficient representation that reduces the number of functions needed while maintaining rendering quality.
AI.method: The solution to the light transport equation is expressed as a 13D Gaussian mixture model. Parameters are directly estimated by minimizing the residual of the rendering equation (rather than using Neumann series). An efficient culling strategy is introduced to handle the computational complexity of evaluating linear combinations of high-dimensional Gaussian functions.
AI.result: Achieves rendering times on the order of milliseconds with a fraction of the memory requirements of conventional neural rendering approaches. Provides view-independent global illumination solutions in real time.
AI.conclusion: The Gaussian mixture model representation with scene properties integrated enables efficient, fast, view-independent global illumination computation with significantly reduced memory usage compared to neural approaches.

title: Learned Continuous Synthesis of Quadratic Difference Tone Spectra
comment: Accepted at the AI Music Creativity (AIMC) 2026 Conference held in Berlin, Germany. 8 pages and 3 figures
summary: Quadratic difference tones (QDTs) are a species of auditory distortion product in which a "phantom" pure tone, absent from the acoustic signal, is clearly audible to listeners. Exploiting this phenomenon, one can synthesize harmonically rich tones for musical purposes, a technique called Quadratic Difference Tone Spectrum (QDTS) synthesis. Previous works have introduced numerical methods to synthesize QDTS based on the distortion function, which links a target QDTS and an overtone-structured carrier signal. While accurate, these methods were stochastic and discontinuous, making them difficult to control for musical purposes and effectively limiting them to stationary signals. This paper proposes a neural network-based approach that learns an approximate inverse of the distortion mapping in an autoencoder-like configuration, producing a continuous approximation that addresses prior limitations. Experimental results show that, although slightly less numerically precise, the method is sufficient for perceptual and musical applications. We also implement a real-time version in Max and evaluate its performance. Various sound examples demonstrate its expressive and musical potential. The source code, audio examples, tutorials, and software accompanying this work are available at https://cordutie.github.io/projects/qdts.html

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a neural network-based method for Quadratic Difference Tone Spectrum (QDTS) synthesis, which creates "phantom" pure tones through auditory distortion products. The approach learns an approximate inverse of the distortion mapping in an autoencoder-like configuration, addressing prior limitations of stochastic and discontinuous numerical methods.
AI.motivation: Previous numerical methods for QDTS synthesis were accurate but stochastic, discontinuous, difficult to control for musical purposes, and limited to stationary signals. The authors sought a continuous, controllable approach suitable for real-time musical applications.
AI.method: The paper proposes a neural network-based approach that learns an approximate inverse of the distortion mapping in an autoencoder-like configuration. This produces a continuous approximation that addresses prior limitations. A real-time implementation was also developed in Max (visual programming environment for audio).
AI.result: Experimental results demonstrate that while slightly less numerically precise than prior methods, the neural network approach is sufficient for perceptual and musical applications. The real-time implementation in Max shows adequate performance, and sound examples demonstrate expressive and musical potential.
AI.conclusion: The neural network-based QDTS synthesis method successfully provides a continuous, controllable approximation that works for musical purposes, though with some trade-off in numerical precision. The availability of source code, audio examples, and tutorials supports further exploration and adoption by the musical community.

title: Zero-shot rib design: merging training-free generative prior with topology optimization
summary: Natural load-bearing patterns such as leaf venation, trabecular bone, and spider webs achieve high stiffness per unit mass, yet classical topology optimizers rarely reach such geometries, and few let engineers express structural design intent through natural language. This work treats a frozen text-to-image diffusion model as a training-free source of design knowledge and distills it into the physics loop of density-based topology optimization via score distillation sampling, so that a text prompt becomes an explicit, machine-interpretable representation of engineer intent. The prompt-induced generative gradient and the finite element sensitivity are combined at every iteration, letting physics decide which prompt-induced features survive. In 245 primary SDS runs spanning four geometric domains and two physics regimes, 38 of 49 prompt--domain combinations achieved statistically significant compliance reductions (up to $-31.5\%$ mechanical and $-23.0\%$ thermoelastic), outperforming gradient-based baselines. Cross-domain morphological analysis identifies a recurring structural signature of improvement: in most domains the generative prior suppresses dead-end branches in the rib skeleton, with endpoint--compliance correlation $r = +0.56$ to $+0.99$. A Heaviside projection with $β$-continuation resolves a pronounced intermediate-density tendency in this diffusion--physics coupling ($42.6\%$ to $<3\%$), and an automated skeleton-based pipeline converts optimized density fields into \rev{candidate geometry ready for computer-aided design. By retargeting the generative prior across domains, loading conditions, and physics objectives through a change of text prompt, with each new problem's physics setup specified separately, the framework uses a pretrained generative model as a reusable, training-free prior for engineering design.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a method that uses a frozen text-to-image diffusion model as a training-free design prior for topology optimization. By combining prompt-induced generative gradients with finite element sensitivity analysis, engineers can express structural design intent through natural language text prompts. The method achieved up to 31.5% mechanical and 23.0% thermoelastic compliance reductions across 245 experiments.
AI.motivation: Natural load-bearing structures (leaf venation, trabecular bone, spider webs) achieve high stiffness-to-mass ratios, but classical topology optimizers rarely produce such geometries. Additionally, existing tools lack the ability for engineers to express design intent through natural language, limiting the integration of intuitive design knowledge into optimization loops.
AI.method: The method treats a frozen text-to-image diffusion model as a training-free source of design knowledge and distills it into density-based topology optimization via score distillation sampling (SDS). At each iteration, the prompt-induced generative gradient is combined with finite element sensitivity, allowing physics to determine which prompt-induced features persist. A Heaviside projection with β-continuation addresses intermediate-density issues, and an automated skeleton-based pipeline converts optimized density fields into CAD-ready geometry.
AI.result: In 245 primary SDS runs across four geometric domains and two physics regimes, 38 of 49 prompt-domain combinations achieved statistically significant compliance reductions (up to -31.5% mechanical and -23.0% thermoelastic), outperforming gradient-based baselines. Cross-domain morphological analysis revealed that the generative prior suppresses dead-end branches in rib skeletons, with endpoint-compliance correlation r = +0.56 to +0.99. The Heaviside projection reduced intermediate-density tendency from 42.6% to less than 3%.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully uses a pretrained generative model as a reusable, training-free prior for engineering design. By retargeting the generative prior across domains, loading conditions, and physics objectives through text prompts, the method enables natural language-based structural design intent expression while maintaining physics fidelity.

title: A Multi-Stage Rule-Chaining Framework for Compositional and Interpretable Cognitive Reasoning
summary:
The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) benchmarks cognitive generalization, the ability to infer and apply abstract rules from limited examples. This paper presents a multi-stage rule-chaining framework that performs compositional reasoning across symbolic, structural, and conceptual levels. The framework integrates three complementary solvers:
  (1) a deterministic rule discovery module that induces atomic transformations through geometric, color, and object-based analysis;
  (2) a pattern-composition engine that reconstructs outputs via block merging, repetition, and spatial heuristics; and
  (3) a structural abstraction layer that infers hierarchical and nested relationships across grids.
  These solvers operate sequentially within a progressive fallback hierarchy, where each stage reuses prior reasoning traces to enhance interpretability and generalization. Training passed for 995 tasks out of 1000, further evaluated on 105 tasks out of 120 and solved 230 test tasks out of 240 ARC-AGI-2 tasks. The system achieved strong coverage across deterministic, compositional, and abstract categories, demonstrating an overall accuracy exceeding 95 percent. The proposed architecture bridges symbolic reasoning and pattern synthesis, providing interpretable insight into cognitive generalization. The results suggest that rule chaining and hierarchical composition can advance machine reasoning toward transparent, human-aligned abstraction without relying on task-specific tuning.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a multi-stage rule-chaining framework for solving ARC (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) tasks, which benchmark cognitive generalization. The framework combines three solvers operating sequentially: (1) deterministic rule discovery for atomic transformations, (2) pattern-composition engine for output reconstruction, and (3) structural abstraction layer for hierarchical relationships. The system achieves 99.5% on training tasks (995/1000), 87.5% on evaluation tasks (105/120), and 95.8% on ARC-AGI-2 test tasks (230/240), demonstrating over 95% overall accuracy.
AI.motivation: The ARC benchmark tests cognitive generalization—the ability to infer and apply abstract rules from limited examples. Existing approaches struggle with compositional reasoning across symbolic, structural, and conceptual levels. This paper aims to address this limitation by developing a framework that can perform hierarchical and nested reasoning without task-specific tuning.
AI.method: The proposed framework uses a progressive fallback hierarchy with three integrated solvers operating sequentially: (1) A deterministic rule discovery module that induces atomic transformations through geometric, color, and object-based analysis; (2) A pattern-composition engine that reconstructs outputs via block merging, repetition, and spatial heuristics; (3) A structural abstraction layer that infers hierarchical and nested relationships across grids. Each stage reuses prior reasoning traces to enhance interpretability and generalization.
AI.result: The system achieved: 99.5% accuracy on training tasks (995/1000), 87.5% on evaluated tasks (105/120), and 95.8% on ARC-AGI-2 test tasks (230/240). Overall accuracy exceeded 95%, with strong coverage across deterministic, compositional, and abstract categories.
AI.conclusion: The proposed architecture bridges symbolic reasoning and pattern synthesis, providing interpretable insight into cognitive generalization. The results suggest that rule chaining and hierarchical composition can advance machine reasoning toward transparent, human-aligned abstraction without relying on task-specific tuning.

title: ReqEvolve: User-Oriented Software Self-Evolution through Automatic Requirement Interpretation
comment: 13 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE 2026), Munich, Germany, October 12-16, 2026
summary: The paradigm of software self-evolution enables systems to autonomously extend and reconfigure their own capabilities during execution in response to technical specifications. Yet requests for new functionality often originate from end users and are rarely expressed in technical terms. As a result, developers must translate user needs into technical specifications before the system can evolve, delaying early validation of the requested functionality by preventing users from immediately observing the resulting behaviour. To address this gap, we present ReqEvolve, a runtime code generation system that enables user-driven self-evolution by accepting high-level user requests. The system integrates automatic requirements engineering (RE) and test-driven development (TDD) to transform these requests into executable functionality through clarification, specification decomposition, test generation, and runtime integration. We evaluate ReqEvolve on 72 software evolution cases across 18 projects against two baselines: SpecFix, an RE-focused code generation approach, and an ablation variant of our system. ReqEvolve achieves 89.2% Pass@1, outperforming SpecFix by 18.8% (p < 0.01, r = 0.79, large effect) and the ablation baseline by 32.6% (p < 0.001, r = 0.88, large effect). These results provide initial evidence that user-driven self-evolution is a viable paradigm for autonomously extending software capabilities from user requests, thereby accelerating requirements validation prior to developer verification.

AI.tldr: ReqEvolve is a runtime code generation system enabling user-driven self-evolution by integrating automatic requirements engineering (RE) and test-driven development (TDD) to transform high-level user requests into executable functionality through clarification, specification decomposition, test generation, and runtime integration. Evaluated on 72 cases across 18 projects, it achieves 89.2% Pass@1, outperforming SpecFix by 18.8% and an ablation baseline by 32.6%.
AI.motivation: To address the gap between user requests (expressed in non-technical terms) and technical specifications required for software self-evolution. Currently, developers must translate user needs into technical specifications before the system can evolve, which delays early validation of requested functionality by preventing users from immediately observing the resulting behavior.
AI.method: ReqEvolve integrates automatic requirements engineering (RE) and test-driven development (TDD) to transform high-level user requests into executable functionality through four key processes: (1) Clarification, (2) Specification decomposition, (3) Test generation, and (4) Runtime integration. The system was evaluated on 72 software evolution cases across 18 projects against two baselines: SpecFix (an RE-focused code generation approach) and an ablation variant of the system.
AI.result: ReqEvolve achieves 89.2% Pass@1. It outperforms SpecFix by 18.8% (statistically significant with p < 0.01, effect size r = 0.79, large effect) and the ablation baseline by 32.6% (p < 0.001, r = 0.88, large effect). Both comparisons show large effect sizes, indicating substantial practical significance.
AI.conclusion: User-driven self-evolution is a viable paradigm for autonomously extending software capabilities directly from user requests. This approach accelerates requirements validation prior to developer verification, enabling users to observe resulting behavior immediately without waiting for developer translation of their needs into technical specifications.

title: MHE-Former: Multi-Hypothesis Transformers via Entropy Maximization for 3D Mesh Recovery
summary: Monocular 3D hand and body mesh recovery often suffers from severe occlusion and ambiguity. Traditional deterministic methods typically regress a single optimal solution, leading to overconfident predictions. In this paper, we introduce an exploration--exploitation paradigm for ambiguous mesh recovery with multi-hypothesis learning and selection. Specifically, during exploration, based on our probabilistic formulation and entropy maximization, we propose a novel multi-hypothesis method referred to as MHE-Former. It is a Transformer-based multi-hypothesis framework, ensuring high training efficiency and label friendliness while generating plausible and diverse hypotheses. During exploitation, we propose Hypothesis Selection, a context-aware process for multiple predictions. Especially leveraging VLM's powerful visual understanding and reasoning capabilities, it allows users to choose the most plausible and desired estimate with additional evidence and natural language intent. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in accuracy and diversity across multiple datasets. The user preference study further shows the practicality of our hypothesis selection process.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses ambiguity in monocular 3D hand and body mesh recovery by proposing a novel exploration-exploitation paradigm with multi-hypothesis learning. The framework MHE-Former generates diverse plausible hypotheses during exploration, while a VLM-based hypothesis selection mechanism allows users to choose the most appropriate output during exploitation.
AI.motivation: Monocular 3D hand and body mesh recovery often suffers from severe occlusion and ambiguity. Traditional deterministic methods regress a single optimal solution, leading to overconfident predictions that fail to capture the inherent uncertainty in the task.
AI.method: The proposed framework consists of two phases: (1) Exploration - MHE-Former, a Transformer-based multi-hypothesis method using probabilistic formulation and entropy maximization to generate plausible and diverse hypotheses with high training efficiency and label friendliness; (2) Exploitation - Hypothesis Selection leveraging VLM's visual understanding and reasoning capabilities for context-aware selection using natural language intent.
AI.result: The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in accuracy and diversity across multiple datasets. User preference study demonstrates the practicality of the hypothesis selection process.
AI.conclusion: The exploration-exploitation paradigm with multi-hypothesis learning and VLM-based selection effectively addresses the ambiguity problem in monocular 3D mesh recovery, providing both accurate and diverse predictions while allowing user-friendly selection of desired estimates.

title: Hologram Representation via Quadratic Phase Gaussian Splatting
summary: We introduce Complex-Valued Quadratic Phase Gaussian (CVQPG), a novel hologram representation method that replaces standard 2D Gaussian representations used in 2D Gaussian Splatting with 2D quadratic phase functions. CVQPG incorporates additional learnable parameters to control the curvature of these bases. We evaluate our approach against state-of-the-art methods, exceeding the visual quality by +0.19 dB (RGB) and +0.33 dB (grayscale) on average in holographic reconstructions. Specifically, our equal parameter count evaluations show that modulating the primitive's wavefront is an effective and lightweight enhancement for hologram representations. In addition, our frequency domain analysis illustrates that CVQPG has successfully preserved the mid-to-high frequency band of natural images.

AI.tldr: CVQPG is a novel hologram representation method that replaces standard 2D Gaussian representations (from 2D Gaussian Splatting) with 2D quadratic phase functions, incorporating additional learnable parameters to control curvature. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods by +0.19 dB (RGB) and +0.33 dB (grayscale) in holographic reconstructions while preserving mid-to-high frequency bands of natural images.
AI.motivation: The motivation appears to be improving holographic reconstructions by enhancing the primitive representation in hologram computing. Standard 2D Gaussian representations used in 2D Gaussian Splatting have limitations in representing wavefronts. By replacing these with quadratic phase functions that can modulate the primitive's wavefront, the method aims to achieve better visual quality in holographic reconstructions.
AI.method: The method introduces Complex-Valued Quadratic Phase Gaussian (CVQPG), which replaces 2D Gaussian representations with 2D quadratic phase functions. Key innovations include: (1) Using 2D quadratic phase functions as basis functions instead of standard 2D Gaussians, (2) Incorporating additional learnable parameters to control the curvature of these basis functions, and (3) This allows modulation of the primitive's wavefront for more effective hologram representation.
AI.result: The approach achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods: +0.19 dB improvement in RGB holographic reconstructions and +0.33 dB improvement in grayscale reconstructions on average. The equal parameter count evaluations demonstrate that wavefront modulation is an effective and lightweight enhancement. Frequency domain analysis shows CVQPG successfully preserves the mid-to-high frequency band of natural images.
AI.conclusion: CVQPG provides an effective and lightweight enhancement for hologram representations by modulating the primitive's wavefront through quadratic phase functions with learnable curvature parameters. The method achieves state-of-the-art visual quality in holographic reconstructions while maintaining computational efficiency through equal parameter counts, and successfully preserves important frequency components of natural images.

title: Xiaomi-CocktailASR-1 Technical Report
summary: Recently, large language model (LLM) based ASR models have achieved significant progress, yet they generally lack support for multi-speaker scenarios, where the cocktail party problem remains a critical bottleneck for further advancing ASR. Existing TS-ASR methods, including end-to-end architectures with speaker embeddings and latest LLM-based explorations suffer from degraded single-speaker performance and the inability to reject when the target speaker is absent. In this paper, we propose Xiaomi-CocktailASR-1, an LLM-based end-to-end TS-ASR architecture. By utilizing reference speech as voiceprint prompts, it directly transcribes the target speaker's speech without requiring speech separation. Xiaomi-CocktailASR-1 maintains competitive performance in single-speaker scenarios, comparable to mainstream ASR models. It also features a negative sample rejection capability, outputting empty text when the target speaker is absent from the mixed speech. Additionally, Xiaomi-CocktailASR-1 supports a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning mode to provide explicit reasoning steps. Extensive experiments on various synthetic and real-world multispeaker benchmarks demonstrate that Xiaomi-CocktailASR-1 achieves state-of-the-art performance, effectively addressing the cocktail party problem through a unified architecture that balances multispeaker and single-speaker recognition accuracy, along with rejection capability.

AI.tldr: Xiaomi-CocktailASR-1 is an LLM-based end-to-end target speaker ASR system that uses reference speech as voiceprint prompts to directly transcribe target speaker speech from mixed audio without requiring speech separation. It maintains competitive single-speaker performance while offering negative sample rejection capability and Chain-of-Thought reasoning support.
AI.motivation: The cocktail party problem remains a critical bottleneck for LLM-based ASR models, which generally lack support for multi-speaker scenarios. Existing target speaker ASR (TS-ASR) methods suffer from degraded single-speaker performance and inability to reject when the target speaker is absent.
AI.method: The proposed Xiaomi-CocktailASR-1 uses reference speech as voiceprint prompts in an LLM-based end-to-end architecture, enabling direct transcription of target speaker speech without speech separation. It supports Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning mode for explicit reasoning steps.
AI.result: The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on various synthetic and real-world multispeaker benchmarks, maintaining competitive single-speaker performance comparable to mainstream ASR models, while also featuring negative sample rejection capability (outputs empty text when target speaker is absent).
AI.conclusion: Xiaomi-CocktailASR-1 effectively addresses the cocktail party problem through a unified architecture that balances multispeaker and single-speaker recognition accuracy along with rejection capability.

title: Byzantine-Robust Federated Fire Detection with a Rotating Coordinator
summary: We study the application of federated learning (FL) to indoor fire detection. Such fire-detection systems use edge cameras that record sensitive footage which cannot easily be collected at a central server. Existing federated solutions leave three practical obstacles unaddressed: limited uplink bandwidth, Byzantine (malicious or faulty) clients, and unconditional trust in a single, permanently fixed aggregation server. Our main contributions address all three. In particular, we provide (i) a curated indoor fire-detection dataset assembled from eight public sources; (ii) an edge-deployable detector whose model updates are compressed up to 10 time with only a small loss in balanced accuracy; and (iii) a semi-decentralized Byzantine-robust FL method that combines history-aware aggregation with a rotating coordinator, evicting stealthy attacks that per-round filters miss while removing the fixed-server single point of failure. On the held-out test set the rotating-coordinator method matches its fixed-server counterpart in accuracy and detection speed, and a physically distributed six-node cloud deployment confirms feasibility.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses three practical challenges in applying federated learning (FL) to indoor fire detection using edge cameras: limited uplink bandwidth, Byzantine (malicious) clients, and reliance on a fixed aggregation server. The authors contribute a curated fire-detection dataset, a compressed edge-deployable detector, and a semi-decentralized Byzantine-robust FL method with rotating coordinator.
AI.motivation: Existing federated learning solutions for fire detection leave three critical practical obstacles unaddressed: (1) limited uplink bandwidth for transmitting model updates from edge devices, (2) vulnerability to Byzantine (malicious or faulty) clients, and (3) unconditional trust in a single permanently fixed aggregation server, creating a single point of failure. Fire-detection systems using edge cameras record sensitive footage that cannot be easily collected at a central server, making FL a promising approach but requiring these practical issues to be solved.
AI.method: The paper proposes three main contributions: (i) A curated indoor fire-detection dataset assembled from eight public sources; (ii) An edge-deployable detector with model updates compressed up to 10 times with minimal balanced accuracy loss; (iii) A semi-decentralized Byzantine-robust FL method combining history-aware aggregation with a rotating coordinator that evicts stealthy attacks that per-round filters miss while removing the fixed-server single point of failure.
AI.result: On the held-out test set, the rotating-coordinator method matches its fixed-server counterpart in accuracy and detection speed. A physically distributed six-node cloud deployment confirms the feasibility of the proposed approach.
AI.conclusion: The proposed semi-decentralized Byzantine-robust FL method with rotating coordinator successfully addresses all three practical obstacles in federated fire detection: bandwidth compression, Byzantine robustness, and elimination of the fixed-server single point of failure, while maintaining comparable accuracy and detection speed to traditional fixed-server approaches.

title: Understanding LoRA Rank Trade-offs in Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at CSCE 2026
summary: Selecting LoRA rank for diffusion fine-tuning requires balancing quality and compute cost.
